7. Source-verification migration.approval_type: Reviewed literal source trust anchor, not a cryptographic signature or automatic approval. Manifest and bootstrap deliberately avoid circular self-hashing; pure current documentation is outside the executable closure.
7. Source-verification migration.bound_inputs: Current runtime pages/modules/shared assets; exact CSS; build/scanner/package/lock/configuration; actual validators, tests, CI coverage/workflow; frozen historical audits/projectors and registry dependencies.
validation_sequence: Check literal manifest/bootstrap identity, expected base and exact seven-page scope.
Read/hash complete current dependency closure and exact HTML route/consumer inventory; validate local head stylesheet and no migrated compiler.
Only after current approval succeeds, reverse enumerated exact operations and verify original source hashes at the starting commit.

7. Source-verification migration.snapshot_architecture: Preservation batches capture one fully validated immutable byte snapshot. Snapshot readers bind the exact repository root/path and reject changed source arguments. They compare captured historical evidence only; they never approve later disk changes. Live checks reread/hash the full closure without cross-call mtime caching, including same-size/same-mtime mutations. Captured old-manifest preimage hashes also reject the frozen historical projector fallback if the old manifest disappears during snapshot preparation.
7. Source-verification migration.normalization: Only CRLF to LF for UTF-8 source; preserve every trailing byte. Binary assets use exact bytes.
7. Source-verification migration.historical_integrity: 254 existing dated audits unchanged; Task 17/SEO Task 2A frozen manifests and original SEO/consent projector implementations preserved. Old overlay-specific tests still operate on reconstructed historical source. No generic source-hash bypass and no refreshed historical hashes.
7. Source-verification migration.future_change: Any approved runtime/build/test dependency change invalidates the current approval and requires explicit new review, record and tests; current on-disk hashes alone are not authority.
7. Source-verification migration.test_fixture_reads: Historical preservation keeps every assertion and fixed Git revision. A test-only bounded Git blob reader avoids repeated Git process startup; it validates requested revisions/paths and returned blob identity/size. It reads immutable Git objects and never approves current working-tree bytes.
